in_arabic.name: رويل
in_arabic.meaning: رويل اسم يعني الحلقة أو الدائرة الصغيرة
in_arabic.long_meaning: رويل هو اسم مشتق من كلمة 'رول' التي تعني الحلقة أو الدائرة الصغيرة، وقد وردت هذه الكلمة في بعض التفاسير القرآنية. يستخدم هذا الاسم في بعض الثقافات الإسلامية للإشارة إلى الشخص الذي يمتلك شخصية دائمة ومستمرة.

in_urdu.name: رویل
in_urdu.meaning: رویل کا مطلب ہے چھوٹا سا دائرہ یا حلقہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: رویل نام عربی زبان کی جڑوں سے ماخوذ ہے، جہاں اس کا مطلب ہوتا ہے چھوٹا سا دائرہ یا حلقہ۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافت میں استعمال ہوتا ہے، جہاں اس کا تعلق روحانی معانی اور دائمی وجود سے ہے۔

in_hindi.name: रोवेल
in_hindi.meaning: रोवेल का अर्थ है छोटा सा चक्र या वृत्त
in_hindi.long_meaning: रोवेल नाम इस्लामी परंपरा में प्रयोग होता है, जिसका अर्थ है छोटा सा चक्र या वृत्त। यह नाम अरबी जड़ों से निकला है और भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में इसका उपयोग होता है, जहां इसका संबंध आध्यात्मिक महत्व और स्थायी अस्तित्व से है।

in_pashto.name: رويل
in_pashto.meaning: رويل د کوچني حلقې يا دايرې معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: رويل نوم د پښتو ژبې د کلتور څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چیرته چې دا د کوچني حلقې يا دايرې معنی لري. دا نوم د افغان او پښتون دودیزو ارزښتونو سره تړاو لري، چیرته چې دا دايمي وجود او روحاني معنا ته اشاره کوي.

data.cultural_impact: The Islamic name "Rowel" is not a common name within the Islamic community as it is not found in the Hadith or Quran. However, the qualities it signifies - kindness and justice - are highly valued in Islamic teachings and essential elements of good character. These virtues are reflective of the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) character and values, making the name a reminder and inspiration for individuals to embody these qualities in their daily lives.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Rowel" can serve as a reminder for individuals to strive for justice in their actions and to be kind and compassionate in their dealings with others. This is in accordance with the Islamic belief in treating others with respect, fairness, and kindness, as these are ethical values that lead to inner peace and spiritual growth. Additionally, the name "Rowel" can encourage individuals to seek joy and happiness through actions that contribute positively to society and promote justice, rather than through personal gain or the harm of others. This reflects Islamic teachings encouraging individuals to contribute to the betterment of society and to strive towards the greater good for all.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's Muqaddimah mentions a chief named Rowel (Ru'l) of the Banu Hilal in the early 14th century. He led the Banu Hilal in a migration from the Arabian Peninsula to North Africa. This migration contributed to the spread of the Islamic faith and the formation of new Islamic states in the Maghreb.

Al-Maqrizi, in his book Al-Mawāʿiẓ wa-l-īʿṭāẓ, mentions that Rowel (Ru'l) was the last chief of the Banu Hilal before they embraced Islam. He was living in the region of Ghadamis (Libya) around 1297. The Banu Hilal were known for their fierce resistance to the Islamic rule, but with Rowel's conversion, they began to accept Islam and gradually integrated into the Islamic society.
